content:
Journalist and author Bob Woodward, who spent decades at The Washington Post and remains an associate editor there, called out the newspaper’s billionaire owner Jeff Bezos for showing up at President Donald Trump’s second inauguration.

“I think it’s important that the owner not take sides,” Woodward told Mike Allen of Axios. “And Bezos, to take that side of showing up at the inaugural, I literally felt sick to my stomach that that had happened, that he would do that.”

Woodward said Bezos, the founder of Amazon and Blue Origin, was sending a clear message with his presence.

“He’s the owner and to show up at Trump’s inaugural, voluntarily, in a very visible way, which is not just, ‘Oh, I’m going to the movies,’ it’s ‘I am blessing and endorsing this man,’” Woodward said, adding:

“And I ’member seeing it and just feeling sick to my stomach... and that I knew Katharine Graham, the owner of the Post during Watergate, would never do anything like that because she wanted the reporting to be hard and fiery and she didn’t want to take sides.”

Woodward and fellow journalist Carl Bernstein broke the Watergate story that ultimately led to President Richard M. Nixon’s 1974 resignation and won The Washington Post a Pulitzer Prize.

He told Allen that he was initially enthused when Bezos purchased the newspaper in 2013.

“I thought this is salvation that’s come,” he said. “And he has tarnished not only his own reputation, but that of The Washington Post.”

Bezos has been far cozier with Trump during his second term in office. Earlier this year, Bezos praised Trump as “a more mature, more disciplined version of himself than he was in his first term.”

In addition to appearing at the inauguration, Bezos also turned up at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort days earlier, and has been a guest at several White House events, including the state dinner with Chinese President Xi Jinping in September.

In addition, Amazon ― where Bezos remains executive chair ― donated $1 million to the inauguration and is listed as a contributor to Trump’s ballroom project. The company has also paid $75 million for production, distribution and promotion of the Melania Trump documentary. At least $10 million of that went to the first lady herself, according to the president’s financial disclosures.

Allen asked Woodward if he’s ever told Bezos his concerns personally.

“I’ve said it publicly,” he said.
